articleTitle: Low-Cost Smart Spectacles to Assist Blind Individuals in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Advancements in assistive technologies present a promising avenue for enhancing the independence and safety of visually impaired individuals, integrating seamlessly into their daily routines and providing essential support for navigating environments. This research introduces a low-cost Smart Glass (Spectacles) for blind people, utilizing an ultrasonic sensor, NE 555 IC, 10 UF 25V capacitor and buzzer. The proposed device excels in non-invasive detection of obstacles, offering real-time auditory feedback to alert users of potential hazards. By incorporating widely available and cost-effective components, the Smart Glass offers an accessible solution to improve the mobility and autonomy of visually impaired individuals, particularly in developing regions. The test results show promising outcomes that may significantly impact personal safety, independence, and overall quality of life.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Microstrip Patch Antenna for Breast Tumor Detection at ISM Band and Tera-Hertz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Breast tumors are currently women's leading cause of death. This project focuses on the development of a compact, comprehensive microwave imaging system for breast tumor diagnostics in real-time. The proposed system utilizes a dual-frequency microwave imaging technique. Firstly, a microstrip patch antenna operates within the frequency range of 100 GHz to 10 THz, with a specific focus at 0.3 THz. On FR-4 (Lossy) substrate, the antenna is tested with and without a phantom. THz antenna performance is greater when a tumor is present in the phantom than in free space. Secondly, four antennas using the ISM band frequency operate at 2.47 GHz, within the 2.42 GHz to 2.48 GHz range, also built on an FR-4 (Lossy) substrate. The CST Studio breast phantom is implanted with a 5mm tumor. For the tumor phantom, the highest return loss values for all four antennas are −20.20dB, −20.21dB, −20.19dB, and −20.17dB. Using the IC-DAS algorithm, 79 frequencies, S parameters, antenna position, and 6 channels are extracted from the CST CSV file and inserted in MATLAB. The system ultimately confirms the tumor's presence, making breast tumor diagnostics more accessible and enhancing healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Optimizing Day-Ahead Charging Schedules for Electric Vehicles: A Multi-Factor Priority-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: With the ever-increasing market for electric vehicles (EVs) it becomes more and more critical to comprehend the potential implications of EV charging on existing distribution network. This paper presents a methodology for optimizing EV charging schedules to mitigate the network overloading issues. User data, including preferred charging time, kWh rating, State of charge (SoC) level, and travel projection, has been used to develop priority factor that helps to determine individual charging needs. The findings reveal that the methodology effectively balances the load across time slots by addressing overloading issues through optimization using Genetic Algorithm (GA). Besides the average to peak demand ratio is increased from 74.5% to 96.4% with this proposed charging scheme. Overall, the methodology integrates user preferences with grid constraints, providing a comprehensive solution for EV charging management that optimizes both energy efficiency and user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Bangladeshi Currency Coin Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In today's dynamic world, accurate recognition of currency coins is crucial for various financial activities, especially for visually impaired individuals who face significant challenges in identifying coins for daily transactions in Bangladesh as most of the Bangladeshi coins are similar in size, shape, and texture. This study aims to address these issues by developing and evaluating deep learning-based models for Bangladeshi currency coin recognition by utilizing convolutional neural networks, specifically the Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) model and standard CNN model using PyTorch. The pretrained ResNet-50 backbone in the Faster R-CNN extracts high-level features such as edges, textures, shapes, and patterns to classify coin images into 14 distinct categories, while the CNN model provides a simpler yet competitive approach. These coin images were captured under diverse lighting and environmental conditions simulating real-world scenarios. Evaluations are conducted on the trained model using a variety of standard and own-recorded datasets, including shifted, rotated, and translated images. We found an average accuracy of 91.18% for Testing dataset and 90.99% for Validation dataset using Faster R-CNN, whereas the CNN model achieves 84.04% and 81.07% accuracy on the Test and Validation sets, respectively.

articleTitle: Designing and Manufacturing of Robo Nurse with Fully Articulating Hand
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper introduces a Robo Nurse designed to remotely monitor patients in hazardous environments, such as those infected with COVID-19. The robot utilizes MAX30100 and GY906 sensors to accurately measure vital parameters like body temperature, oxygen level, and heart rate. Equipped with a fully articulating hand, the robot can navigate hospital environments and perform tasks with minimal human intervention. Preliminary results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system for real-time remote patient care, offering a promising solution to enhance healthcare safety in high-risk areas. Future work will focus on integrating automated navigation capabilities using Raspberry Pi to further reduce human contact with patients.

articleTitle: A Detailed Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithm Performance in Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Human deaths are natural events, but heart disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Predicting heart disease using machine learning can significantly benefit global health, though it presents clinical challenges requiring high accuracy and efficiency. Many countries face a shortage of cardiovascular experts and a high rate of misdiagnoses, which can be mitigated by accurately determining the stage of coronary disease and supporting medical decisions with automated patient records. This paper addresses the prediction of coronary disease based on input attributes using data mining techniques. The results showed that the CatBoost Classifier achieved the highest accuracy at 87.2%, followed closely by the Ridge Classifier at 86.3%. Other models, such as XGBoost and Gradient Boosting, performed similarly, achieving 84.0%, while the RandomForest Classifier had a slightly better performance with an accuracy of 85.6%.

articleTitle: Novel Design of a Circular Patch Antenna for 5G Communication Embedded Body Centric Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: A microstrip circular patch antenna is designed for on-body communication in this paper. The antenna's structure is a slightly circular-shaped radiator and the coaxial feed technique is used for improving the performance of antenna parameters like return loss, efficiency, gain etc. rather than used for microstrip line feeding technique. The CST Microwave Studio Suite, a well-liked and dependable electromagnetic simulation program running on Microsoft Windows, was used to build and simulate the antenna. A resonant frequency at 3.5 GHz, 7.56 dBi of gain, and 96% efficiency, is found through free space simulation. Every characteristic of this suggested antenna, including VSWR, bandwidth, S-parameter, and reflection loss, has been identified and shown. Additional parametric analyses show that by enlarge. It was intended to be used with the Body Centric Network (BCN). To evaluate its human on-body performance, a virtual three-dimensional human torso phantom was created, and the results were recreated by placing the antenna near it. The antenna was placed at five different distances from the human torso model to perform a distance-based investigation into the effects of the presence of the human body. The results were contrasted with one another and free-space models to determine how distance impacts its behaviors. Despite the variable distance, the on-body simulations gave very consistent findings with a small deviation. According to distance-based research, the antenna should be kept more than 2 mm (about 0.08 in) away from the human body for the best performance.

articleTitle: Research on Advanced Control Strategies for Building Energy Management Systems to Optimize Energy Consumption in Commercial Buildings by Using DRL-PC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This study investigates the application of Deep Rein-forcement Learning combined with Predictive Control (DRL-PC) algorithms in Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS) for commercial buildings in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The research compares the performance of a DRL-PC algorithm against a traditional rule-based control system in a 10-story office building over a 12-month period. The DRL-PC algorithm demonstrated significant improvements, achieving a 21 % reduction in annual energy consumption, a 25 % increase in occupant comfort sat-isfaction, and a 28% reduction in peak energy demand. The system showed remarkable adaptability to Dhaka's challenging climate, maintaining optimal indoor conditions 92 % of the time. With a payback period of 2.7 years, the proposed system offers a promising solution for enhancing energy efficiency and occupant comfort in commercial buildings, particularly in regions with complex climatic conditions.

Author Keywords: deep reinforce-ment learning combined with predictive control (DRL-PC) algorithms

articleTitle: Electro Deposition of Copper on the Mild Steel Substrate and Investigation of its Different Properties
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This research investigates the influence of bath composition on the current efficiency microhardness and morphological properties of the deposited copper layer. We explore the impact of varying concentrations of each bath constituent on these aspects to optimize the deposition process. We found the highest current efficiency and lowest microhardness when we used the highest concentrations of Copper Sulphate. We also observed the current efficiency and microhardness for different concentrations of Sodium Chloride, Sulphuric acid and Polyethylene glycol (PEG). We obtained highest current efficiency and microhardness when we used lowest concentrations of Sodium Cloride, Salphuric acid and PEG. Surface morphology of the deposited copper is analyzed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). SEM analysis is expected to reveal the morphology of the copper film, while EDX will confirm its elemental composition. The surface morphology of Cu deposited mild steel reveals that the Cu particle is uniformly deposited and somewhere clusters are found. The deposition is also confirmed by EDX spectra where the atomic and weight percentage of Cu were found 95.42% and 84% respectively. This research aims to establish optimal deposition parameters for achieving the desired properties of electrodeposited copper on mild steel substrates.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Short Circuit Current Limit on Damping Phenomenon for Different PV Penetration Levels
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper presents a transient analysis of the frequency response in a power system under four different scenarios. The study considers the integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and the utilization of a Static Var Compensator (SVC), each leading to distinct frequency response behaviors during pre-fault, fault, and post-fault conditions. The results demonstrate that the frequency response remains within the permissible limits defined by the UK's grid code, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards. Additionally, the inclusion of PV integration introduces significant damping effects, which can be effectively mitigated by incorporating an SVC rated at 150% of the inverter's short circuit current or by increasing the inverter's short circuit current to 200% of the rated value. These findings provide valuable insights for managing frequency response in power systems with PV integration, enabling system operators to maintain stable and compliant operations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Transformer Maintenance Schedules Based on Fault Prediction Models
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In the pursuit of enhancing the reliability and costeffectiveness of power transformer maintenance, this paper introduces an optimized maintenance scheduling methodology based on Reinforcement Learning (RL). By modeling the maintenance scheduling problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), the proposed RL framework aims to minimize the cumulative operational costs while maximizing transformer reliability over time. Through a series of hypothetical simulations, the RL-optimized maintenance policy is compared against traditional time-based schedules, demonstrating a significant reduction in costs and an improvement in reliability. The results confirm the robustness and adaptability of the RL approach, highlighting its potential application in real-world transformer asset management.

articleTitle: Improved Breast Cancer Detection in Ultrasound Images Using Masked Image Integration and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: An early diagnosis is essential for the effective treatment of breast cancer, which is one of the most commonly prevalent cancers in women. In this study, we propose a Deep Learning Transfer Learning technique for segmenting breast cancer tumors from Ultrasound images. To enhance efficiency, we also added masked images with the ultrasound images as a novel strategy. Our main goal is to produce better outcomes with fewer images. To begin with, a straightforward CNN model is created to segment the tumors. To segregate the tumors from the ultrasound and masked images, we next examine how well several Pretrained models, including VGG16, ResNet50, XceptionNet, EfficientNetB7, and ConvNeXtBase, perform. Using metrics like as Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1-score we evaluate each model's performance. Our findings demonstrate that transfer learning-based approaches perform better than the straightforward CNN model in terms of Accuracy and F1-Score, and that using masked images in addition to the ultrasound images enhances performances even more. EfficientNetB7, which has an F1-Score of 0.9750 and an overall Accuracy of 97.50%, is considered the best-performing model. Importantly, our method only requires a modest quantity of training data to produce these outcomes.

articleTitle: Development and Performance Analysis of Darrieus and Savonius Turbines Using QBlade
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In this research a vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT-Darrieus type) is designed and optimized using QBlade software based on three design parameters. Three types of airfoils have been chosen to find out the suitable design to make three-bladed Darrieus type VAWT. A Savonius type VAWT was developed practically to characterize the developed generator coupling arrangement. This Darrieus type was simulated and optimized using Qblade. A practical test was done to compare the electrical and mechanical power, thrust of both turbines using a wind tunnel. After simulation, it was found that the Darrieus type VAWT with 1 meter height, 0.75-meter radius and 0.075-meter chord length with 75° circular angle made by “DU 06-W-200” airfoil has better coefficient of performance. On the other hand, the Savonius type VAWT having 0.37 meter and a radius of 0.11 meter showed 0.0006 Watt electrical power and 5.8844 Watt mechanical power at 4 m/s. Savonius type wind turbine with 0.37 meter height and 0.11 meter radius is applicable for low speed whereas larger 1 meter Darrieus type could be the proper choice.

articleTitle: Delta/Fork Transformer Based 30-Pulse Star Rectifier for Input Current Harmonic Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper proposes a delta/fork transformer-based 30-pulse star rectifier for large current and low voltage applications. The proposed rectifier comprises two 15-pulse parallelly connected uncontrolled star rectifiers connected to the load through an inter-phase transformer (IPT). The Delta/fork type transformer is designed and optimized to produce two sets of 15-phase power supplies that supply the power to the two 15-pulse star-connected rectifiers. This analysis demonstrates that the proposed rectifier effectively suppresses up to the 29th-order harmonics from the input line current. Remarkably, the total harmonic distortion (THD) of both input line current and voltage remains below 5% even under varying load conditions. This research contributes to finding efficient power conversion and offers practical insights for industrial applications. The proposed rectifier finds its suitability in scenarios where isolation is essential. Notably, it serves applications such as aluminum potlines, traction substations, graphitizing furnaces, zinc electrolysis, and AC drives. Rigorous analysis, design, modeling, and MATLAB-based simulations validate the proposed design. The proposed rectifier meets the requirements of the IEEE-519 standards. This research contributes valuable insights into industrial power systems.

articleTitle: Assessing the Societal Impact of Internet Blackouts in Dhaka: A Multidimensional Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Internet blackouts cause significant disruptions across society, affecting various domains. This research investigates the impact of a 13-day internet blackout in Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 2024, focusing on its economic, academic, and mental health consequences. Also, this study emphasizes the multifaceted societal consequences of internet blackouts and highlights the critical need for resilient digital infrastructures and effective contingency strategies. A comprehensive survey was carried out to evaluate the impact of internet blackouts on various demographic groups, including students, professionals, business owners, freelancers, and homemakers. The results found significant financial losses among business owners and freelancers, which contributed to a decline in GDP and national reserves. Students faced major academic disruptions, while widespread stress and anxiety brought mental health concerns to the forefront. Additionally, the blackout caused severe interruptions in communication, travel, and professional opportunities. Homemakers, although less affected financially, struggled with maintaining communication during the disruption. The research offers critical insights to guide policymakers in protecting essential online services and strengthening societal resilience against future crises.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Patch Antenna with High Gain for WiMAX and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The microstrip patch antenna was specifically designed to be operational at a frequency of 7.8 GHz for applications in WiMAX and X-band satellite communication. The proposed design utilized a patch with optimized dimensions on Rogers RT/duroid substrate with a permittivity of 2.2 and a thickness of 1.5 mm. The patch of the antenna comprised two patch elements that were connected to each other. Adding the second patch enhanced the antenna's performance by improving its return loss to -49.92 dB and VSWR to 1.006 along with achieving an optimal gain of 8.5 dB. The antenna demonstrated a resonant frequency of 7.8 GHz with a stable radiation pattern, low return loss (-49.92 dB), low VSWR, and high gain of about 8.5 dB.

articleTitle: Skin Tumor, Lipoma and Cyst Detection by Graphene Based on-Body Patch Antenna in L Band
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Body-implanted antennae are a popular and costeffective approach to dragonize sickness promptly. Early detection of a medical condition makes treatment easier and may possibly save the patient's life. The primary purpose of this work is to develop an on-body patch antenna for biotelemetry. The largest organ is the skin, which covers the whole surface of the body. Skin problems have become more frequent all over the world in recent years. Nobody has ever lived a life without facing difficulty. The primary purpose of this study is to detect skin cysts, lipomas, and malignancies by identifying the S1,1 parameter of a microstrip patch antenna using cutting-edge materials such as graphene. Graphene is a recently discovered material with extremely high electrical conductivity and resistance. To achieve this, an on-body microstrip patch antenna was built utilizing four different types of skin disease models: normal skin, tumor-affected skin, lipoma-affected skin, and cyst-affected skin. The skin disease detection antenna was developed in the L-band (1.18 GHz). The antenna and four skin phantom models in the CST Studio Suite have been used to provide a range of outputs, including return loss, voltage standing wave ratio, far-field, and directivity. Return loss was found to be −33.3908 dB for a skin tumor, −33.3915 dB for skin lipoma, and −33.3876 for a skin cyst, compared to −33.3993 dB for normal skin. This antenna has a Specific Absorption Rate of 1.42 W/kg, making it bio compactable.

articleTitle: Analyzing Risk Level from RoI and VoI for Robust Data Privacy using Fuzzy Inference System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In the modern digital environment, securing data privacy has become increasingly critical as organizations confront rising threats from cyber-attacks and data breaches. To safeguard sensitive information, businesses must invest in robust data protection measures, yet balancing these investments with their potential benefits remains challenging. This research addresses this issue by proposing a novel framework that integrates Return on Investment (RoI) and Value of Information (VoI) within a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) to assess data privacy risks effectively. RoI measures the financial return relative to the cost of data protection investments, indicating the economic value derived from such measures. VoI, on the other hand, evaluates the worth of the information protected by these investments, reflecting its impact on decision-making and operational efficiency. By employing a FIS, which accommodates uncertainties and imprecise data, this framework provides a nuanced approach to risk assessment, enabling organizations to optimize their data privacy strategies. The integration of RoI and VoI within the FIS allows for a comprehensive evaluation of risk levels, facilitating more informed decision-making and improved risk management. This research aims to enhance data privacy practices by offering a methodical and adaptable tool for evaluating and balancing investments in data protection.

articleTitle: A Simple Approach to Zero Crossing Detection of Voltage and its Application in Distributed Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Turning on and off the relays at or near the zero-crossing point of the supply voltage is essential for their reliable and safe operation, as well as for minimizing disturbances in current and voltage waveforms. This paper presents two innovative software approaches for detecting zero crossings in distributed power supply systems, which are crucial for enhancing voltage regulation and minimizing disturbances in voltage and current waveforms. By enabling precise relay operations at zero crossing points, these methods not only improve system stability but also protect relays from potential malfunctions. The versatility of these approaches is highlighted by their compatibility with a universal voltage range of 85–265 V and frequencies of 50 Hz or 60 Hz, requiring minimal hardware for implementation. Additionally, the methods facilitate frequency measurement, which allows for the assessment of other critical parameters such as voltage, current, power, power factor, and energy consumption. The paper also introduces a frequency measurement technique capable of detecting islanding in grid-connected systems, further enhancing the reliability of power supply systems. Validation of these methods using the PSIM® simulator demonstrates their effectiveness and ease of implementation, as they can be executed through straightforward coding. One of the approaches also takes into account the aging process of the components.

articleTitle: A Correlative Abstraction Between the Scenario of No-Retransmission and Retransmission Process by Utilizing Evolutionary Game Theory for Self-Organized Data Aggregation Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Successive data connectivity is very important for delivering data from one point to another. But sometimes there is no successive data connectivity between the two points. A delay tolerant network (DTN) is one of the best ways to provide data connectivity with no end-to-end connection using self-organized data aggregation techniques. Here, a better strategy (to become sender or aggregator) is selected by the Evolutionary Game Theory approach. Special Data Custody Nodules (called Aggregators) are responsible for keeping and holding data until the message ferry visits and collects data from aggregators to deliver it to sink nodules. This message ferry approach is only applicable where there are multiple clusters involved. The choice of strategy-deciding between becoming an aggregator or a sender-is examined using the principles of Evolutionary Game Theory. In this context, each nodule assesses its outcomes following interactions with others. To facilitate strategy selection, we can utilize different ordinances from Evolutionary Game Theory, such as the Imitation Reform Ordinance, along with the Birth-Death and Death-Birth Reform Ordinances with two different processes named by no retransmission and retransmission. In this recent paperwork, we will compare these two processes for plan of action with the Imitation Reform Ordinance, Birth-Death, and Death-Birth Reform Ordinances.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Smart Grid Stability Using Diverse Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The increasing integration of diverse energy sources within smart grids has introduced new challenges for maintaining grid stability. Traditional stability evaluation techniques often fail to address modern power systems' energetic and nonlinear nature. The proposed study explores the application of machine learning algorithms, including Random Forests, XGBoost, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Logistic Regression, to predict smart grid stability. A comprehensive dataset of 60,000 samples representing various grid scenarios was utilized, and the models were assessed using precision, accuracy, recall, and F1-score metrics. Among the tested models, XGBoost showed superior performance, with the highest accuracy of 97.93% across various conditions. This result underscores the potential of machine learning in enhancing grid reliability, reducing the risk of power outages, and supporting the integration of renewable energy sources. By advancing predictive analytics in smart grid systems, this approach contributes to developing more resilient and adaptive energy networks, essential for meeting the demands of a sustainable future.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy-Based Battery Storage Swapping Station for Electrical Vehicles and Net Metering
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Most of the electricity used for normal charging of EVs is generated from fossil fuels, which pose a number of problems to The surroundings and power grid, restricting access to charging. Due to increasing demand in EVs, proper development of a robust charging infrastructure is urgently required to eventually ensure widespread adoption. Simultaneously, this puts additional pressure on local electricity grids, and hence combining affordable and sustainable energy sources such as solar power also poses a pressing need. In tune with the above requirement, this paper attempts the innovation of sustainable energy infrastructures and swapping battery stations for EVs. This may include the use of solar panels, power storage systems, and advanced net metering techniques so that proper capturing and storage of solar energy may be possible on site. Later on, the stored energy will not only be used for charging of EVs but also will help in grid durability by net metering, and thus, a sustainable and robust charging infrastructure will be developed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fringe Visibility and Film Thickness Relationship of an Optical Fiber CO2 Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The thickness of a Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) cavity plays a vital role controlling the intensity, absorbance, and fringe visibility of the FPI at a particular wavelength. In this work, an FPI-based optical fiber CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor (OFCS) was simulated for the film thickness range of 4.88-7.23 μm (achieved from a few scanning electron microscope images of an OFCS). The absorbance peak was achieved at a wavelength of 600 nm. The normalized intensity decreases by 86.7 %, absorbance increases by 35.1 %, and fringe visibility decreases by 3.31 % at around 600 nm for rising the film thickness from 4.88 μm to 7.23 μm, The difference between practical and simulated fringe visibility was monitored. So, the idea of the desired output can be achieved by simulating the mathematical model of an FPI-based optical fiber sensor before performing the lab experiments.

articleTitle: Impact of Battery Operated Three Wheeler on Local Grid System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the impact of battery-operated three-wheelers on the local electrical grid in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The study employs a modified sensitivity analysis algorithm tailored to Dhaka's unique environmental and infrastructural characteristics. By analyzing factors such as charging capacity, energy consumption, and ambient conditions, we assess the grid's stability and the potential challenges posed by the rapid adoption of electric three-wheelers. The results indicate significant increases in peak load, voltage deviations, and overall energy demand, necessitating strategic grid management and potential infrastructure upgrades. Fur-thermore, the study highlights the environmental and economic benefits of transitioning to electric mobility, showcasing the potential for substantial reductions in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and long-term cost savings. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and grid operators aiming to ensure sustainable urban transport electrification.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based Non-Invasive Framework for Neurodegenerative Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis from Template-Less Handwritten Shapes
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder affecting millions globally. Current diagnostic methods lack precision. In this research, an approach combining Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) with a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for early PD diagnosis is proposed. A medical image dataset was curated, and preprocessing techniques were employed for image enhancement and uniformity. The CNN extracts key features while HOG provides edge orientation information, and their fusion creates a robust feature map. An integrated attention mechanism further refines focus on crucial regions. Evaluation demonstrates a balanced performance in terms of accuracy (99%) and parameter (0.8M) requirement. Visualization tools like GradCAM offer insights into model decisions, aiding interpretability. This approach offers an accurate PD detection, potentially transforming diagnosis and improving patient outcomes. Code will be made available at https://github.com/rifanawal99/P-DL.

articleTitle: Improving the Stability in Intensity and Absorbance of an Optical Fiber CO2 Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Achieving the stable intensity response of an optical fiber CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor (OFCS) is challenging due to film cracking and humidity. In this work, two OFCSs (OFCS 1 and 2) were fabricated without and with Triton X-100, and the differences in stability were observed after storing these for 35 days. Also, the stability of an OFCS was monitored without and with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) cast film. The absorbance at 600 nm decreases from 0.41 to 0.18 for OFCS 1 without Triton X-100, whereas the absorbance at 600 nm fluctuates between 0.82 and 0.84 for OFCS 2 with Triton X-100 within a storage period (9–35 days). The reflection intensity at 600 nm reduces by 12.4 % and only 0.82 % for an OFCS without PTFE film and with PTFE film, respectively, for the relative humidity increment between 50 % and 70 %. Triton X-100 and PTFE film successfully showed the absorbance and reflection intensity reduction at 600 nm for the OFCS.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Four-Port MIMO Antenna for Enhanced Terahertz Communication and Multifaceted Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: A novel graphene four-port Terahertz (THz) MIMO antenna is introduced that aims to revolutionize Terahertz communications with its multifaceted applications. The proposed design utilizes complementary microstrip patch elements. This compact antenna, designed on a silicon substrate of 80 × 80 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, boasts a wide impedance bandwidth of 1.28 and 2.56 THz. By utilizing a complementary microstrip patch between radiating elements, a significant reduction is achieved, resulting in isolation levels of -70 dB. The performance of the design is compared to that of a basic patch antenna to highlight its benefits. The proposed MIMO design, thoroughly analyzed in terms of its key attributes, offers several advantages, including a wide 0.6 THz bandwidth, a directivity of 3.62 dB, compact size, and consistent radiation characteristics. The antenna's attributes render it perfect for an extensive array of THz band uses, such as IoT, biomedical applications, and rapid 6G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis of Solar Thermal System Installation for Sanitary Hot Water Requirements in a Residential Building
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Existing studies on solar thermal systems for residential complexes often face challenges in achieving a balance between energy generation, cost-effectiveness, and environmental impact. This paper investigates the feasibility of a solar thermal system for meeting the Sanitary Hot Water (SHW) demand in a residential complex. The study addresses these challenges by evaluating the potential of solar thermal energy in comparison to other renewable energy sources. The analysis focuses on an existing residential complex located at Heriot Watt University, Edinburgh, where the roof space available for solar collectors is limited to 150 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed system consists of 58 flat-plate vertical collectors, which were selected based on this available area. The system is projected to generate 8,217 kWh in June and 2,193 kWh in November, offsetting the energy demand in June and approximately half of the demand in November. A 30kW auxiliary boiler is proposed to cover the remaining energy deficit in November. The environmental benefits of the system include a reduction of 7.7 tons of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions annually, by replacing gas-fired boilers. With an initial investment of £32,000, which includes the cost of collectors, heating system, and installation, the system offers a payback period of 12.5 years when factoring in annual savings from reduced gas consumption.

articleTitle: WSe2-Based Bi-Metallic SPR Refractive Index Sensor with Enhanced Sensing Properties
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The surface plasmon resonance (SPR) method is a novel and precise measurement approach for sensing applications. Here, a tungsten diselenide (WSe2) based bimetallic SPR refractive index (RI) sensor has been modeled and designed utilizingLumerical Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) platform. The angular interrogation method has been employed to generate SPR response by varying refractive index (RI) of analyte and it is captured by the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) monitor. The sensor exhibits an enhanced sensitivity of 210 deg/Refractive Index Unit (RIU) with quality factor and detection accuracy of 225.80/RIU and 1.13 respectively. The sensor showed a broad sensing range for RI ranging between 1.33 to 1.36. Furthermore, the distribution of electric field is analyzed for the developed structure and the peak intensity is found at WSe2/analyte interface having a penetration depth of about 122 nm. Thus, the sensor could be utilized in the field of healthcare and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of an Intelligent Single-Axis Solar Tracking System for Optimized Solar Energy Collection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In the era of declining conventional energy, 39.5% of solar energy is used in total energy consumption as a reliable, sustainable, and renewable energy source in Bangladesh. A tracking system helps to maximize the collection of solar energy. Solar arrays and trackers align with the Sun's daily east-west and seasonal north-south movements and provide more electricity than fixed panels. An intelligent solar tracker uses a linear actuator and tracks the solar radiation by not sensing the radiation but instead tracking the Sun's location. This research presents the design and construction of a single-axis solar tracking system employing a linear actuator, which enhances the efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) panels by maintaining their alignment with the Sun's position throughout the day. The system is configured without Light Dependent Resistors (LDRs), allowing it to operate successfully even in gloomy weather by tracking the Sun's location rather than its beams. The setup incorporates a microcontroller, a motor driver, and a power supply to control the linear actuator. Initial experimental results demonstrate that the system can incrementally adjust the solar panel's angle, ensuring maximum sunlight absorption and significantly improving energy output. The proposed solar tracker, active from 7 am to 5 pm, adjusts the panel's position at calculated intervals, potentially increasing the efficiency of single-axis trackers beyond conventional systems. This development holds promise for enhancing the practicality and performance of solar energy systems in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Dynamic Load Forecasting in EV Charging Systems Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Load forecasting is crucial for efficient power system operations, particularly with the raising usage of electric vehicles (EVs) and fluctuating energy demands. However, traditional forecasting methods often fail to address the non-linear patterns and temporal dependencies in EV charging data, leading to inefficiencies in grid management and energy optimization. This study develops a deep learning-based algorithm using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional LSTM (Bi LSTM) networks to enhance the accuracy of EV charging load predictions. A comprehensive dataset from EV charging stations in Palo Alto was preprocessed with outlier removal, temporal feature extraction, and normalization, while Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied for dimensionality drop. Results reveal that BiLSTM outperformed LSTM, achieving lower RMSE (0.1806) and MAE (0.1588) by effectively capturing bidirectional temporal patterns. Correlation analysis identified time-related variables as critical predictors, further improving forecast precision and scalability. This approach optimizes EV charging, integrates renewable energy, supports grid stability, and provides a robust solution for advancing energy management within the growing EV infrastructure, addressing the rising complexities of modern power systems.

articleTitle: Implantable Sinusoidal-Shaped Antenna for Body Centric Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper presents a unique design of an implantable antenna with a sinusoidal-shaped patch radiator that operates in the 2.4 GHz Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. To avoid discomfort for the subject, the substrate material has been chosen as a flexible one, Rogers RO3210, with a high dielectric constant of 10.8. The wavy shape and high relative permittivity aided in its miniaturization. A preliminary calculation conducted in free space results in an impedance bandwidth of 212 MHz and a return loss of over 21 dB around 2.41 GHz. In addition, an artificial human body model with layers of muscle, fat, and skin was created digitally, and the antenna was placed 4.2 mm within the muscle layer to do in-body analysis. In in-body circumstances, the antenna yields intriguing findings, similar to those observed in free space. The radiation pattern antenna performs well, and it might be used in implantable applications without a major divergence in characteristics like the reflection coefficient, gain, and directivity. The design could be a potential candidate for in-body applications under body centric wireless communication (BCWC).

articleTitle: Production Cost and Emissions Minimization Based on Renewable Energy Using Superiority of Feasible Solutions- Moth Flame Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper introduces a refined version of the Moth Flame Optimization (MFO) algorithm, Superiority of Feasible Solutions-Moth Flame Optimization (SF-MFO), in recognition of the significant influence of renewable energy on both production costs and secretion reduction in energy structure. To improve the symmetry among scrutiny and fleecing also to resolve the limitations of the early MFO, SF-MFO implements two significant enhancements. The algorithm's objective is to reduce emissions and optimize production costs by utilizing renewable energy sources, resulting in a combined reduction in both. Its primary intention is to decrease the total operating expense of the production system, as well as to address active power loss, voltage deviations at load buses, and the cost and emissions of combined units. The SF-MFO is analyse on IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 118-bus structure by transforming this multi-objective problem into a single-objective function with specific constraints and utilizing a bus location index to refine the list of candidate buses. The effectiveness and benefits of the suggested SF-MFO are then highlighted by contrasting the outcomes with those of other published algorithms.

Author Keywords: Superiority of Feasible Solutions-Moth Flame Optimization

articleTitle: Dual-Band Implantable Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The following work proposes the architecture and analysis of a unique implantable antenna. The design is engineered for biomedical applications within the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. Its performance was studied at 2.4 and 5.8 GHz through simulations conducted in free space and in-body environments. The primary aim was to develop a cost-efficient, high-performance antenna characterized by a small form factor and an affordable substrate, ensuring its suitability for medical applications. The design features a unique steering wheel-shaped patch fabricated on a Rogers RO3010 substrate, with copper as the conductive substance for both the patch and the ground plane. The antenna measures 30 × 22 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and employs a partial ground plane to enable dual-band resonance powered by a 50 Ω microstrip feed. Simulation results demonstrated resonance at 2.4 and 5.8 GHz, with bandwidths of 400 and 270 MHz, respectively. The Voltage Standing Wave Ratios (VSWR) were measured at 1.20 for 2.4 GHz frequency and 1.25 for 5.8 GHz frequency. Additionally, the antenna's gain, directivity, and radiation patterns validated its effectiveness for implantation within the human body. The simulations were executed using the CST Studio Suite software, showcasing its potential for biotelemetry and other medical applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Optimization and Performance Evaluation of Lead-Free BaZrS3-Based Perovskite Solar Cells with Consideration of Structural and Operating Parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Lead-free BaZrS3 is considered a highly promising substitute for lead-based halide perovskites. This research involved designing and simulating a perovskite solar cell using the Glass/ITO/ZnO/BaZrS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O/Ni structure. Zirconium halide perovskite was employed to address lead halides' stability and toxicity issues. The solar cell's performance was evaluated using the one-dimensional simulation program SCAPS-1D. The analysis focused on essential parameters such as absorber thickness, absorber defect density, hole transport layer (HTL) thickness, HTL acceptor density, electron transport layer (ETL) thickness, ETL donor density, and operating temperature. At a current density (JSC) of 21.49 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.37 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 89.98%, the results indicate a maximum efficiency of 26.53%. These results establish the possibility of creating ecologically sustainable and highly effective PSCs using barium zirconium sulfide (BaZ<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>S3).

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Ge and InP MOSFETs in High Current Applications with SiO2/Al2O3/Ga2O3 Gate Oxides
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This study analyzes the performance of Germanium (Ge) and Indium Phosphide (InP) MOSFETs with various gate oxide materials: SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> for high drain current applications. The paper develops a numerical model in COMSOL Multiphysics to simulate MOSFET behavior with these oxides, analyzing their impact on device performance. Results demonstrate that Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> offers the highest drain current and lowest threshold voltage among the oxides tested, significantly outperforming SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Specifically, Ge MOSFET with Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> exhibits drain currents up to 7397 μA, while InP MOSFETs with Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> reach up to 6245 μA. The study compares these findings with existing research, highlighting the advantages of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in optimizing high-current MOSFETs. The findings of this study suggest that Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in Ge MOSFET is a promising candidate for enhancing the performance of high-current applications, particularly when compared to traditional gate oxide materials.

articleTitle: A Novel MPPT Algorithm for Different PV Array Arrangements: Horse Herd Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In order to meet the growing demand for power while lowering the emissions of harmful gasses, photovoltaic (PV) systems are becoming more favored. However, several variables can affect the PV systems, including variations around the global maxima (GM), sluggish response in tracking, and being trapped in local maxima (LM). Alongside this, tracking maximum power point (MPP) for different PV array arrangements is a big challenge. To deal with these issues, a MPP tracker has been implemented using a novel technique known as horse herd optimization (HHO). In this study, the HHO results have been compared with the P&O and Spline MPPT techniques. For all the cases, HHO accurately tracks the MPP with smaller tracking time, higher efficiency, and zero oscillation whereas the P&O accurately tracks MPP only for the second case and Spline trap at LM for the first case and tracks MPP accurately for the second and third cases. For the second and third cases, Spline takes much time, 0.24sec and 0.45sec respectively to settle at GM whereas HHO takes only 0.07sec and 0.27sec respectively. The average tracking efficiency of HHO was 99.9 percent.

articleTitle: A Transmission Gate Based BCD To Seven-Segment Decoder with a Power Consumption of 6.03626 $\mu \mathrm{W}$
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In digital electronics, Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) to Seven-Segment Decoders are essential tools for converting BCD input into an output seen on a seven-segment display. This paper undertakes a comparative analysis of the proposed system utilizing 45nm bulk MOSFET technology through three different methods: Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS), Pseudo NMOS Logic and Transmission Gate. A detailed analysis and comparison of the design process and important aspects of each technique is conducted, with a particular emphasis on important metrics such as propagation delay and power consumption. After a successful comparison, it can be concluded that transmission gate based technology achieves the best performance in power consumption, measured at 6.03626 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex>. Additionally, it demonstrates a frequency of 126.87 MHz and a propagation delay of 200.41 ns. Furthermore, we conducted three sign-off processes, for example, Layout Versus Schematic (LVS), Electrical Rule Checking (ERC) and Design Rule Checking (DRC) tests, revealing a layout area of 406.1686 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> using the transmission gate technique. To validate the proposed design, we carried out (Process, Voltage, and Temperature) PVT Corner analysis & Monte Carlo simulation in Cadence Virtuoso.

articleTitle: A Smart Tutor Avatar for Mimicking Characters of Bangla Sign Language
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: A smart tutor avatar teaches Bangla Sign Language (BSL) by mimicking its 49 characters, pro-viding a visual and immersive learning experience to bridge communication gaps for the hearing-impaired. This research introduces a novel avatar system designed specifically for BSL, enhancing the learning process through interactive and engaging methods. The avatar uses machine learning and image processing to analyze hand gestures and replicate BSL signs, creating an interactive learning tool. Initial dataset preprocessing trains the system to produce accurate sign visuals. The user interface is intuitive, allowing learners to engage in physical exercises to improve sensorimotor skills, with immediate feedback provided via cosine similarity. While avatar tutors have been explored for American Sign Language, this study is pioneering in its approach to BSL. The proposed research has the potential to make BSL learning more accessible and enjoyable for a wider audience.

articleTitle: Research on Optimizing Demand Response Programs using LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing Demand Response (DR) programs using Long Short-Term Mem-ory (LSTM) networks. We propose a methodology that leverages LSTM's capability to handle sequential data for accurate load forecasting and DR strategy optimization. Our approach integrates smart meter data, weather information, and socio-economic factors to enhance prediction accuracy. We implement a Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Price Control (DRL-PC) algorithm for DR optimization. The results demonstrate significant improvements in forecasting accuracy, with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 4.02%. The proposed method achieved energy savings of up to 3.06% per month, with cumulative savings fluctuating throughout the year. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and reliable demand response strategies, promoting grid stability and sustainability in smart energy systems.

articleTitle: THz-BA: Terahertz Antenna Design for Biological Applications with a Focus on Riboflavin Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In this work, we have designed a terahertz antenna for riboflavin detection. Three layers make up the structure of the microstrip antenna: the bottom layer models the ground plane, the middle layer models the substrate, and the top layer models the rectangular patch. The antenna design employed a FR4 substrate with a thickness of 1.7 μm and a dielectric constant of 4.3. The copper material used for the ground plane, feed line, and patch has a thickness of 0.00035μm. The suggested configuration offers an omnidirectional radiation pattern with a gain of 5.662 dBi. The antenna operates in two frequency bands. Two frequencies have been identified: the first is 2.3361 THz to 2.4622 THz with a bandwidth of 0.12605 THz, and the second is 4.4986 THz to 4.8711 THz with a bandwidth of 0.3725 THz and projected antenna return loss of −21.088dB and-21.427dB. At 2.40 THz and 4.75THz, the antenna resonates. Thus, the aforementioned antenna can be used for biological purposes, such as riboflavin detection.

articleTitle: Production of 3D Printing Filament from Recycled Plastic Bottles using Fused Deposition Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This study focuses on establishing a sustainable and innovative approach to recycling low-density polyethylene (LDPE) derived from waste plastic bottles. The release of millions of tons of waste plastic into landfills, oceans, and ecosystems around the globe has resulted in plastic pollution as a global environmental crisis. The capital city Dhaka in Bangladesh sees over 600 tons of plastic waste every single day of which less than 36 percent are reused. This study focuses on recycling these plastics into high quality filament materials that can be used for 3D printing. Fused deposition modeling (FDM) is used for making the filament from waste plastic bottles. The study involves various processes such as collecting and sorting LDPE, shredding, washing, drying, melting, extrusion, and quality control measures to ensure the produced filament meets the required standards. Special attention is given to color variation, adaptability to different 3D printers, and the promotion of environmental benefits by complying with the global sustainability goals (SDGs). As the first of its kind in Bangladesh, the study shows the way to not only lessen the burden of plastic trash but also produce handy products and foster a circular economy.

articleTitle: EV Charging Framework: Enhancing Urban Charging Infrastructure with SOC and Emergency Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Aiming at the current scenario, there is an upward trend in the market share of electric vehicles in the global transportation sector. For EV users, charging station scheduling is a must, as users' needs should be considered along with various factors that will initialize the priority for charging in a station. Based on the day-ahead scheduling strategy, a distributed charging scheme is proposed along with priority for emergency vehicles. While scheduling EVs, the State of Charge (SOC) and distance between stations in a typical urban area have been taken into consideration. Also, a well-planned shifting of EVs in between slots and to nearby charging stations is introduced here. Day-ahead user can easily book their slot as they prefer. However, in case of an emergency in real time a day-ahead user will be shifted to another free slot from that day. Also, the paper introduces a priority among emergency vehicles. Here the system is developed using exploratory data analysis (EDA), which is done by fundamental Python (Pandas library).

articleTitle: Applying Heuristic Algorithms for Solving the 0–1 Knapsack Problem: An Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This study analyses and compares the performance of six heuristic algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Simulated Annealing (SA), Hybrid (SA+GA), Tabu Search (TS), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in achieving the optimal solutions to combinatorial optimization problems represented by 0–1 Knapsack Problem (KP01). The algorithms were analyzed based on evaluation metrics like runtime, iteration time, performance, and complexity. The results indicate large differences in runtime efficiency and iteration speed. For runtime and iteration performance Tabu Search was the fastest with the lowest median runtime, followed by PSO and then GA. On the other hand, the average runtime for ACO is the longest and the highest standard deviation. The average time per iteration ranges from 0.027 ms for SA, to 70.8 ms per iteration for ACO which is very efficient. However, the hybrid method is competitive but provides a longer average time per iteration. Despite the variability, SA, GA, and PSO showed competitive results that can derive their robustness for combinatorial problems. These findings underline several key trade-offs and help to choose an optimal heuristic method that is robust and efficient for real-world decision-making applications.

articleTitle: A Wide Range and Highly Linear ISFET Readout Circuit
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The article introduces a highly linear readout circuit for ion-sensitive field-effect transistors (ISFET) developed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.8 \mu \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology. The proposed circuit comprises only eight transistors and a resistor, providing wide input ranges with high linearity. Simulation results from the LTSpice application indicate that the proposed circuit can function across a wide input range of 0.6-3.1 V. It exhibits a sensitivity of 38.3 mV/pH and a linearity of 0.9994 when simulated with a power supply of 3.3 volts. The power consumption rate is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34.42 \mu \mathrm{W}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Advanced Power Quality Management Through a PID-Based Dynamic Voltage Restorer
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Voltage sags caused by faults in power systems pose a significant challenge to maintaining power quality and stability. This study investigates the performance of a Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) equipped with a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller in mitigating voltage sags. Simulations in MATLAB Simulink optimization demonstrate the effectiveness of DVR model in restoring nominal voltage levels during double-line-to-ground (DLG) faults. The DVR compensates for voltage sags by injecting corrective voltage, ensuring uninterrupted power delivery and stability. Analysis of input voltage and RMS voltage behavior shows a rapid recovery from a severe sag of ±100 V to nominal levels of ±325 V and 230 V RMS, respectively. The PID controller ensures smooth recovery without overshoots or oscillations, validating the precision level of the proposed model. The findings underscore the critical role in maintaining reliable power quality under fault conditions of DVR system, highlighting its potential as a robust solution for voltage sag mitigation in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Peltier Cooling System for Photovoltaic Thermal Management Using Simulation Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Mitigating the adverse effect of high temperature on photovoltaic (PV) module's efficiency in hot environment by using a thermoelectric cooling (TEC) method with PV through a detailed analysis, is the pivot objective of this paper. This research evaluates the Peltier module's effect on the power output and temperature of the PV modules in different ambient situations for the active cooling mode of the Peltier module. We utilized PVsyst and MATLAB (for initial circuit designs), as the simulation tools to analyze the performance ratio (PR) and thermal loss factor of the PV system for both with and without cooling conditions. Moreover, under an ambient temperature of 25.2°C, our developed TEC system enhances the PV module's performance ratio ranging from 83.42% to 85.8%, while The thermal loss factor is decreased ranging from −10.36% to −6.7%. These findings indicate that controlled cooling is capable of considerably improving PV performance, resulting in significant energy output rise. In addition to creating new paths to achieve more effective and sustainable energy production, this study demonstrates the way TEC systems might enhance solar energy systems, specifically in hot environments.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Silicon Carbide MOSFETs Using Silicon Dioxide and Silicon Nitride Gate Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The demand for advanced power electronics is driving the development of more efficient and reliable semiconductor devices. This study investigates the impact of different gate dielectric materials, specifically silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), on the performance of silicon carbide (SiC)-based MOSFETs. SiC has emerged as a superior substrate for high-power, high-frequency applications due to its wide bandgap, higher breakdown voltage, and better thermal stability compared to traditional silicon. Using finite element analysis through COMSOL Multiphysics®, this research compares key parameters such as electron mobility, terminal current, and threshold voltage in MOSFETs with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> gates. The results demonstrate that while SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> provides smoother modulation of dopant concentrations and electron flow, Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> exhibits stronger control over electric potential and carrier distribution, resulting in enhanced switching speed and efficiency, Specifically, Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> demonstrated a 15% higher terminal current and a 0.2V reduction in turn-on voltage compared to SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the SiC MOSFET and stabilizing threshold voltage. These findings contribute to the optimization of wide-bandgap semiconductor devices, offering insights for improving MOSFETs in next-generation power systems.

articleTitle: A 64.48GV/s, 5.095uW 4-bit Transmission Gate Based Irregular Sequence Counter in 45nm Process Node
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: A 4-bit irregular sequence counter is a digital circuit that tallies clock pulses, producing a non-sequential 4-bit output. This paper presents a 4-bit irregular sequence counter design that utilizes four JK flip-flops with interconnected outputs and inputs, aiming for simplicity and minimizing component requirements. Comparing among 3 different design methods which include CMOS, Pseudo Logic, and Transmission Gate, the proposed Irregular Sequence counter has been built using the Transmission Gate among the Three for its overall better performance. The Rigorous Cadence simulations at 45 nm technology confirm practical viability by accurately demonstrating sequence generation. A 27.78 ps rise time, 21.78 ps fall time, 20.05 ps propagation delay, 50.04% duty cycle, 9.67 MHz frequency, 64.48 GVs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> slew rate, and 5.095 µW dynamic power and a small layout area of 55.11 nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have been achieved from the proposed design. This paper also presents the PVT corner analysis and Monte Carlo simulation of the design. As the proposed Irregular sequence counter has low power consumption, it can be an ideal candidate for digital signal processing units.

articleTitle: Effect of Artifact Removal in Machine Learning Based Anxiety Screening Using EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Anxiety is among the most prevalent mental health disorders. An essential component of anxiety treatment is screening. The limitations of conventional screening methods can be solved by employing machine learning to identify anxiety from EEG signals. As EEG is nonstationary, artifacts can easily corrupt the signal. The artifact in EEG data needs to be eliminated to enhance signal quality and obtain accurate analysis. The impact of artifact reduction from EEG signals for the machine learningbased anxiety screening was investigated in this study. Here, the EEG data of 40 participants (aged between 18 and 25 years) was used; of these, 24 had anxiety and 16 did not. A novel algorithm for artifact removal was used to process the data. After extracting the Hjorth parameters, the SVM classifier was used. The study revealed that implementing artifact removal improves the classification accuracy of the left frontal channels by 14.67% and the right frontal channels by 8.31% along with other performance parameters.

articleTitle: CNNRF-Ensemble: A Multifaced Approach For Predicting White Spot Syndrome Virus In Shrimp Farming
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Shrimp farming has traditionally served as a crucial source of seafood and revenue for coastal countries, filling the rapid growth demand, especially in Bangladesh. However, the White Spot Syndrome Virus(WSSV) creates and constantly threatens the global shrimp population, impacting the economic and ecological systems. Recently, researchers have tried to predict disease, but no studies have achieved significant accuracy using ML and DL algorithms. In this study, we have proposed an optimized CNNRF-Ensemble model for predicting WSSV using multifaceted data, including geographical features, environmental attributes, farm characteristics, operational practices, and socioeconomic indicators. Our proposed model achieved 95.714% accuracy in sequential model and afterwards, combining with RandomForestClassifier in Ensemble learning we obtained 99.99% accuracy. Our study suggested deep learning as an accurate, easy and low-cost method to predict shrimp WSSV, which helps to predict viruses and create awareness of shrimp firming.

articleTitle: An Intelligent SCADA System for Power Distribution Network Cable Fault Detection with Real-Time Monitoring and Autonomous Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems are significant for boosting industrial operations, but established systems often struggle with fault management and real-time monitoring. To address these issues, this paper proposes an advanced SCADA system that integrates IoT technologies, multi-agent systems, and predictive maintenance for seamless data collection, analysis, and decision-making. Machine learning enhances fault detection and cybersecurity, while a modular hardware design allows scalability and flexibility to various industrial environments. The system is highly sensitive to detecting faults, including open circuit faults, line-to-ground faults, line-to-line faults, double line to ground faults and three-phase faults. It improves operational safety and efficiency by accurately locating faults and notifying professionals in real time. Extensive simulations and hardware tests were conducted to validate its performance in different fault scenarios. The results show that the proposed SCADA system has successfully detected different types of faults, offering a unified approach for fault management, maintenance, and real-time monitoring.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Navigation for the Visually Impaired: A Laser-Based Night Vision Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This study proposes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based system to aid visually impaired individuals by classifying road surfaces. Leveraging image analysis and processing techniques, the model uses laser beams to identify road types under different conditions, including low-light scenarios. The challenge faced by visually impaired people in navigating roads with traditional white canes limited in scope and effectiveness motivated this research. The system incorporates a custom dataset of over 3000 high-quality images, employing contour detection to recognize obstacles and road types from various distances. The model achieves an accuracy exceeding 99% indicating reliability. This advancement offers a significant improvement in navigation and safety providing a practical solution for enhancing mobility and independence for visually impaired users. Future work will focus on expanding the model to detect additional objects further enhancing user safety and environmental awareness.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Real-Time Data Monitoring of a Green House Farm with Offline Monitoring Capability
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Greenhouses have transformed modern agriculture by precisely managing the environmental conditions of delicate plant species to promote crop growth. A conceptual and practical framework for a low-cost greenhouse farm monitoring system has been proposed in this paper to track real-time data on greenhouse farms with online and offline both monitoring capabilities. The Internet of Things (IoT) technology has been used to develop a system prototype, which uses two sensors to collect data on environmental factors, including temperature, humidity, heat index, and soil moisture. An ESP32 microcontroller module collects and sends this sensor data to a Raspberry Pi 4 microcomputer, which displays it on a web application. The application is hosted on a local Raspberry Pi server and built with Node.js, a JavaScript runtime environment. The communication between ESP32 and Raspberry Pi is established with REST API (Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface), a way to connect applications and components in microservices architectures. A highly robust PostgreSQL-based database is used to store the data in Raspberry Pi, which allows the collection of farm data locally without having to connect to any web storage. With an internet connection, data can be monitored from anywhere worldwide using a global server made of Vercel, a cloud-based platform that can host websites and web applications. The local Raspberry pi server would be accessible to the internet through SSH (secure shell) tunneling with Ngrok, a cross-platform application.

articleTitle: A Lightweight CNN Model for Detecting Brain Tumors using MRI Based Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The brain responsible for managing thoughts, mem-ories, movements, and emotions, is the body's most critical organ but is vulnerable to tumors, particularly as we age. These tumors can cause structural changes and lead to life-threatening conditions, such as brain cancer. Early detection is essential for effective treatment and prevention of fatal outcomes.
