While CT and MRI scans are currently used to detect brain tumors, they still require expert analysis to pinpoint their exact location. To streamline and enhance the efficiency of tumor detection, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based approach for analyzing MRI scans. Our model is designed to classify three types of brain tumors-pituitary, glioma, and meningioma-as well as cases with no tumors. Using gray scaling, One-hot encoding, and other preprocessing techniques, we developed a customized CNN model that processes 6484 segmented MRI images for training and testing. We tested the performance of seven pretrained models-Vgg16, Vgg19, ResNet50, InceptionV3, DenseNet-121, and MobileNet-on this dataset, achieving testing accuracies of 93.37 %, 92.42 %, 75.38 %, 91.48%, 94.89%, 23.30%, and 96.02%, respectively. Additionally, we created an ensemble model using all these architectures, resulting in a training accuracy of 91.36% and a validation accuracy of 91.29%. Our customized CNN model outperformed all others because of its architecture and proper hyperparameter tuning, achieving a testing accuracy of 98.11%. With significantly lower time complexity, our model can make reliable decisions in a short period, offering a fast and cost-effective solution. Despite integrating various parameters to manage adverse conditions, the system remains lightweight and efficient. In conclusion, our CNN-based approach provides superior accuracy and speed, making it a viable tool for early brain tumor detection.

articleTitle: Optimizing Sustainability and Cost Efficiency in Distribution Network Through Optimal Switching
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Due to increased demand and the deregulation of power networks, utilities must continue to provide stable, high-quality services in order to maintain operations and reduce electricity rates. This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing sustainability and cost efficiency in distribution networks by optimizing the switching configuration using Mixed Integer Second Order Cone Programming (MISOCP) with tie switching. The study focuses on minimizing power losses and voltage fluctuations, which are critical challenges in maintaining efficient and reliable operation of distribution systems. The proposed method is applied to the IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus systems, demonstrating significant improvements in network performance. By strategically optimizing the tie switches, the method achieves a reduction in power losses by 36.66% for the IEEE 33-bus system and 25.5% for the 69-bus system compared to their initial configurations. These improvements directly contribute to lowering electricity rates and enhancing the overall operational sustainability of the distribution network. The results show that MISOCP is an effective and robust optimization tool for addressing the complexities of distribution network reconfiguration, leading to improved energy efficiency and reduced operational costs.

Author Keywords: Mixed Integer Second Order Cone Programming

articleTitle: Enhanced 360 Degree Cognitive Awareness for Heavy Vehicle Drivers Through Haptic Feedback
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This research explores the use of haptic technology in heavy vehicle driving safety, focusing on its potential to enhance driver assistance systems and improve driving experience. The study addresses driver-induced causes of traffic accidents, including drivers' inability to see around the vehicle due to its length and height. The proposed system provides 360-degree cognitive awareness through haptic feedback, which can improve road safety and mitigate challenges in diverse driving conditions. By using haptic feedback, the driver will be able to get a tangible sense of the presence of objects surrounding the vehicle. Through a comprehensive review of existing literature and experimental studies, the research demonstrates the potential of haptic feedback in revolutionizing the driving experience. The findings highlight the optimum mapping between sensors and vibration motors positions on the human body

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control System Using Object Detection Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In Bangladesh, most four-legged intersections use a static-timed or manually-controlled traffic signaling approach, which creates irrefutable congestion and requires human involvement. This paper proposes an adaptive traffic control system utilizing the YOLO object detection framework within CNNs to address this issue. The system captures and frames images using cameras facing every road at a roundabout to detect and count vehicles in real-time for providing lights based on the traffic conditions, prioritizing emergency vehicles such as ambulances, firetrucks, and police-car while also maintaining queues. It sets the signal duration considering road condition. Using a dataset of 10,462 images across 12 classifications of automobiles and a transfer learning approach in YOLOv8, the model achieved a mAP50 score of 0.90. This automated method reasonably enhances traffic flow management by dynamically adjusting signal lights without human intervention.

articleTitle: Enhanced Economic Load Dispatch in Smart Grid Through Pelican Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The efficient management of Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) in microgrids is crucial for optimizing energy costs, maintaining grid stability, and integrating renewable energy sources. This paper proposes a method of enhancing the ELD in a multi-microgrid system using the Pelican Optimization Algorithm (POA), tested on IEEE-14 bus system. Here, the objective function includes reduction of line losses, optimization of cost efficiency and reserve generation, enhancement of grid stability, and maximization of power generation for achieving optimal ELD. Further performance of the proposed POA method for ELD enhancement is compared with Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Additionally, POA provides enhanced operational stability with lower variability in power output and maintenance costs, making it a superior choice for optimizing microgrid operations. The results highlight that POA outperforms MFO, achieving a 45.4% reduction in power generation costs and a 56.3% increase in power output for certain units. Moreover, the comparative analysis underscores the superiority of POA in managing microgrid operations, offering a promising solution for future energy management challenges.

articleTitle: NoSQL Database Selection Process: An Integrated Proof of Concept and Comparison for Targeted Document Store Databases
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The study offers an analysis of NoSQL document store databases focusing on MongoDB, Couchbase, and CouchDB and includes an integrated Proof of Concept (POC) along with a research-based comparison. It begins with an overview of the evolving landscape of Database Management Systems (DBMS) highlighting the role of NoSQL databases in overcoming the limitations of traditional relational databases. The research includes a contextual evaluation and qualitative comparison of the three databases incorporating performance metrics to gauge their suitability for various applications. MongoDB is identified as the best in query performance (1.5 ms), transaction support, and integration with cloud platforms. Couchbase shows competitive scalability and good query performance (2.6ms) while CouchDB lacks ACID transactions, optimization, and support barriers and shows query time (6 ms), This analysis highlights each database's strengths and weaknesses providing key insights for real-world deployment.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Fuzzy Logic Controlled MPPT Technique for PMSG-Based Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The adoption of renewable energy sources is critical in addressing global energy challenges by providing sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels. Wind power stands out among these due to its vast availability and minimal environmental impact. Wind turbine technology is examined in relation to its application to renewable energy systems, emphasizing the efficiency of energy capture and conversion from the turbines. The pitch can be adjusted dynamically for optimal orientation in the wind, and the mechanical energy is transferred swiftly using gear boxing and electrical conversion with the aid of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG). Measurement of electrical parameters like RMS at Times as soon as possible and implementing challenging control approaches, such as Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), guarantees dependability regarding system stability as well as its ability to perform under fluctuating climate conditions. The proposed Fuzzy Logic Controlled-Maximum Power Point Tracking (FLC-MPPT) algorithm has been evaluated to have a peak power tracking efficiency of above 92.6% and a power tracking efficiency of around 95.7%. With a power output of 240 W, this method enables the efficient utilization of wind energy, contributing to green electricity supply networks and supporting the fight against climate change.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Diabetes Data in Healthcare System Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Diabetes, influenced by factors like high blood pressure, aging, obesity, and poor lifestyle choices, has become a significant health issue, increasing the risk of heart disease, kidney disease, stroke, and other serious conditions. Traditional diagnostic methods in hospitals can sometimes be misleading, underscoring the need for big data analysis in healthcare. This approach can uncover hidden patterns in diabetes-related data, enabling more accurate predictions of outcomes. This paper aims to classify large diabetes datasets to predict the disease's behavior using various attributes. A machine learning model with sixteen classifiers, fine-tuned through k-fold cross-validation, was developed to ensure optimal results, with accuracy measured by F1 score, precision, and recall.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of an IR-Based Automation System with Telegram Bot Integration for Remote Device Control
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Automation is advancing rapidly, with infrared (IR) communication being a key method for controlling electronic devices. Despite this, challenges remain in optimizing IR controllers for consistent performance across varying angles and task loads. A 3D design and a robust algorithm have been developed to enhance the system's accuracy, while security is ensured by matching a unique TOKEN with the Telegram bot for each session. Error rates were analyzed across different angles, with specific zones determined based on performance. Minimal error rates defined the working zone, while higher rates indicated critical and invalid zones. Error rates increased as the transmitter moved further from the optimal angles, such as a 0–6 % error rate when operating within a 0° - 5° range. Reaction time was calculated across multiple tasks, showing an average of 5 seconds per command. Mismatch rates, observed during higher task loads, rose sharply when handling many tasks. For instance, the mismatch rate was 0 % for 12 tasks but 20 % when executing 20 tasks. Performance evaluations demonstrated optimal IR signal strength for reliable control within a distance of 10 to 15 inches, with diminishing effectiveness beyond 20 inches. These findings provide a foundation for developing more reliable and efficient IR control systems for practical applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Microgrid Energy Security Through Optimal Power Sharing in Multi-Modal Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Microgrids (MGs), which combine distributed energy resources (DERs) with energy storage systems (ESS), offer improved energy security, reliability and sustainability by utilizing renewable energy sources for subsequent use. However, single ESS options often face challenges such as short life cycles, low power density etc. More than one ESS can resolve the mentioned issues though it increases complexity and maintaining stability becomes an issue. This paper proposes an effective energy management strategy between two ESS namely battery and supercapacitor to increase energy security in MG. The proposed strategy is designed in such a way that one of the two ESS stays connected all the time to the DC bus to ensure uninterruptable power supply to loads. Due to the use of DC bus, the system complexity decreases as there is no need to control frequency. Two cases were considered to verify the performance of the proposed energy management strategy in Matlab/Simulink. In the first case, during the unavailability of supercapacitor, the battery supplies 50 W to the load in addition to PV whereas supercapacitor supplies 136 W in the absence of battery along with PV. Furthermore, it was shown that the absence of PV has no negative effect in terms of power flow by ESS to meet load demand.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Software Bugs
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Software Bug Prediction (SBP) is essential to control overall software quality. As systems become complex, faults increase, and early prediction is needed to enhance quality and reduce expenses. This paper provides a technical study of thirteen Machine Learning (ML) techniques for predicting software bugs by utilizing NASA's Promise Repository datasets. The study examines the effectiveness of these classification techniques focusing on evaluation metrics such as Precision, Recall, F-measure, Accuracy, Error Rate, FPR, FNR, ROC, and MCC. The results indicate that Random Forest (RF) achieved the highest accuracy on PC1 (94.96%) and CM1 (96.60%), while Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) scored 85.6% on KC1, and Logistic Regression (LR) got 86.25% on KC2. Regarding error rates, RF had the lowest on PC1 (0.050), LR on KC2 (0.137). For FPR, SVM, MLP, LR, RBF, ANN, and AdaBoost excelled on PC1 (0.00). For FNR, Decision Tree (DT) performed best on PC1 (0.611), KC2 (0.518), and LDA on CM1 (0.500).

articleTitle: Advanced Modeling and Simulation of a Concentrating Solar Power Plant with Thermal Energy Storage in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper provides an indepth simulation and optimization analysis of a 100 MWe concentrating solar power (CSP) plant with parabolic trough collectors (PTC) and thermal energy storage (TES) in Dinajpur, Bangladesh. Utilizing the System Advisor Model (SAM) developed by NREL, the study assesses the operational and economic feasibility of the plant in the local weather conditions. The plant experiences seasonal fluctuations in Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) between 5 and 5.5 kWh/m2/day, which significantly impacts its energy production, peaking at 26 GWh in March and reducing to 12 GWh in December. The efficiency of the plant fluctuates between 0.41 and 0.18 due to these variations. The analysis also points out greater thermal losses in colder months and a higher demand for water during warmer periods. Through optimizing the solar multiple (SM) and TES settings, there was a significant decrease in the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE), from 11.52 cents/kWh to 6.21 cents/kWh. The simulation results show the necessity of customizing CSP plant designs to specific local environmental conditions to improve efficiency and sustainability. The study also confirms that deploying a 100 MWe PTC CSP plant in Dinajpur would greatly benefit in achieving energy independence and support the wider integration of renewable energy technologies in Bangladesh, thereby fostering long-term environmental sustainability and reducing dependency on fossil fuels.

articleTitle: Experimental and Computational Analysis of Biogas Yield and Pyrolysis Oil Production from Waste Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The growing global demand for sustainable energy and effective waste management has intensified interest in renewable energy technologies, particularly those that convert organic and plastic waste into valuable energy resources. This study addresses the challenges of optimizing biogas production from organic waste and pyrolysis oil extraction from plastic waste, aiming to enhance process efficiency and scalability. The research combines experimental setups and computational simulations to systematically analyze biogas production from cow dung and cooking waste, as well as pyrolysis oil production from polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS). MATLAB Simulink was employed to simulate biogas production, revealing that cooking waste yields a higher biogas production rate and methane content (up to 65<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) compared to cow dung. Pyrolysis simulations using DWSIM, supported by experimental data, identified polyethylene as the most efficient plastic for oil production, achieving an 82% conversion efficiency. The results deepen the understanding of waste-to-energy processes, aiding in efficiency improvement and industrial scaling.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Autonomous Microgrid Using Osprey Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal size for an autonomous microgrid to satisfy the electrical load demand. The microgrid will comprise many different configurations, such as photovoltaic module, diesel generators, and energy storage technologies. By considering operational constraints to optimize the cost of energy (COE) and life cycle cost (LCC), the Osprey optimization algorithm (OOA) is applied. Furthermore, identify the most economically feasible technology that will ensure a continuous power supply, an economic study of three different energy storage technologies-namely, batteries, hydrogen storage systems, and supercapacitors-is also conducted. Additionally, provide a case study of Manpura island microgrid that validates the proposed approach. The results show that the OOA method in terms of optimal system performance and convergence speed, the loss of power supply probability is set at 0%, the LCC is $196915, the COE is $0.2959 $/kWh, and the amount of GHG is 430 kgs/year.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Ensemble and Supervised Models for Software Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) is one of the significant activities for the quality and reliability of software systems. Ensemble learning techniques have recently become very popular because they combine the strength of more than one base Machine Learning model to achieve improved accuracy. In this study, we compared an ensemble-based approach for SDP with individual base models. We applied a robust ensemble model by combining Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machines. Then, we evaluate the performance using 5 public datasets from NASA's Promise repository and compare the results against the different individual models. Results validate that our ensemble approach has higher accuracy (up to 94.60%), precision, recall, and F1 score than most of the standalone models. We will give insights on the superior performance of the Ensemble model for SDP tasks. Our results underline the potential of ensemble learning in improving software defect prediction.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance of Support Vector Classifier Through Hyperparameter Optimization for Electrical Fault Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Electrical fault detection and classification is crucial for the safety, stability and reliability of the power system. Accurate classification helps to identify fault types, enabling faster restoration of service. In this research work, a model is proposed based on support vector classification (SVC), with significantly higher evaluation metrics compared to other existing model for transmission line fault classification. After optimizing the hyperparameters of support vector classification (SVC), a 99.3% accuracy rate was achieved. A cross-comparison of the evaluation metrics for different algorithm has been presented to validate the selection of SVC over other algorithms. Also, the evaluation metrics of SVC, both before and after hyperparameter optimization, are compared and analyzed to justify the effectiveness of hyperparameter tuning in SVC.

articleTitle: Enhancing 6G Network Performance by Reducing Signaling Load via Distributed Open RAN and SDN
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The exponential expansion of mobile communication traffic, fuelled by a rising number of smart devices and sophisticated applications, has put significant pressure on existing cellular network architectures. The 6G networks need creative ways to meet these difficulties effectively. This study offers a Distributed Open Radio Access Network (DO-RAN) architecture that uses Open-RAN and Software-Defined Networking (SDN) to reduce signalling burden and boost network performance. DO-RAN improves responsiveness, reduces signalling load on the 5GC, and reduces backhaul congestion by decentralising key functionalities such as the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) and the Session Management Function (SMF) from the 5G Core Network (5GC) to the Open-RAN framework's Central Units (CUs). Our proposal compares DO-RAN to Central Open RAN (CO-RAN) and other architectures, such as 4G LTE networks. The findings show that DO-RAN considerably reduces signalling load in a variety of situations, such as network- and user-triggered service events. This architecture provides enhanced efficiency and scalability for 6G cellular networks in addition to meeting the growing demands for signalling.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Women Safety Device Using Haversine Formula
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Women's safety is an urgent concern, and this paper introduces an IoT-based safety device designed to provide real-time monitoring and rapid emergency response. The device integrates sensors for heart rate and body temperature, GPS for location tracking, and GSM for sending alerts. A key innovation is the use of the Haversine formula to calculate the nearest police station, enabling faster response times during emergencies. The system automatically triggers alerts when vital thresholds are crossed, such as a heart rate exceeding 220 BPM or temperature surpassing 40°C, ensuring swift action. Testing confirmed high accuracy in detecting abnormal vitals, with heart rate measurements closely aligning with certified medical devices. Practical tests also validated successful emergency alert transmission and continuous real-time monitoring through cloud integration, making the device a reliable solution for women's safety in critical situations.

articleTitle: Smart Savior: A Life Jacket Integrated IoT Emergency Response System Utilizing TTGO T-Call ESP32 and Advanced Sensor Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Life jackets are crucial for aquatic safety, preventing drowning and aiding in rescue. However, locating survivors can be challenging. The Smart Savior life jacket, enhanced with IoT technology, integrates advanced sensors into a wristband and jacket to monitor environmental and physiological data. Key components include the NEO-6M GPS module, heart rate and body temperature sensors, and the ESP32 microprocessor. Data is transmitted via ESP-NOW for real-time monitoring and analysis. Rescue teams access a dynamic dashboard to prioritize rescue efforts based on geolocation and critical health indicators. The system's performance, evaluated against industry standards, shows faster GPS connectivity, real-time data synchronization, and improved accuracy in heart rate monitoring (98%) and water temperature sensing (±0.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>C). This integration offers a robust and effective approach to enhancing safety and responsiveness during aquatic disasters, making it a vital tool in saving lives.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Systems: Analytic Comparison of Fuzzy Logic and ML Methods for Applying Maximum Power Tracking Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in solar power systems for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is increasingly popular due to the limitations of traditional MPPT methods in locating the global maximum power point (GMPP) under partial shading conditions. Unlike conventional techniques, AI-based algorithms excel at identifying the GMPP even when multiple local maximum power points (MPPs) exist. Compared to traditional methods, AI-based MPPT techniques like reinforcement learning and fuzzy logic typically offer higher efficiency, reduced steady-state oscillation, and faster convergence but require significant resources and investment. This paper compares two AI-based MPPT methods-Fuzzy Logic and Reinforcement Learning using simulation. Each AI approached its strengths and weaknesses, complicating on optimal method selection. It provided a detailed efficiency comparison of these AI methods by implementing them in a solar power grid system under various environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Using VGG16
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The early perception of brain tumors is a crucial endeavor for neurologists and radiologists. Identifying and segregating brain tumors from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans is a strenuous, time-intensive process susceptible to delusion. To overcome these obstacles, this study introduces a deep learning-based framework that utilizes the VGG16 architecture for improved brain tumor perception and codification. The system categorizes MRI images into four distinct groups: glioma, meningioma, pituitary, and no tumor. To enhance the quality of input data and minimize overfitting, advanced preprocessing techniques, including resizing, normalization, and data augmentation, were employed. The VGG16 model, fine-tuned using hyperparameter optimization and transfer learning, extracts critical features to ensure accurate classification. A thorough evaluation on diverse datasets demonstrated the model's robust performance, achieving an validity of 96% while excelling in precision, recall, and F1-score. By addressing challenges related to limited dataset size and computational complexity, this study presents a scalable and automated approach for accurate tumor detection, significantly improving diagnostic efficiency and enabling timely clinical interventions.

articleTitle: Signaling Load Reduction in 5G Network Based Using Open-RAN Architecture and SDN
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges associated with signaling load in 5G Core (5GC) by proposing innovative architectural solutions based on Open Radio Access Network (Open-RAN), and Software-Defined Networking (SDN). The work introduces two novel approaches, Partially Distributed Open RAN (PDO-RAN) and Fully Distributed Open RAN (FDO-RAN), aiming to optimize network performance and efficiency by reduce the signaling load on 5GC. The architectures involve the strategic relocation of critical components, such as the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) and Session Management Function (SMF) from 5GC to the gNB Central Unit (gNB-CU) within the Open RAN architecture. The research conducts a comprehensive evaluation of these proposed architectures, comparing them with the traditional Central Open RAN (CO-RAN), and existing LTE designs. Signaling load analyses, particularly during the initial attachment event, reveal that FDO-RAN consistently outperforms other architectures, showcasing its efficiency in handling signaling processes. The study provides valuable insights into the scalability and effectiveness of distributed and fully distributed Open RAN architectures, offering crucial guidance for future advancements in 5G network optimization.

articleTitle: Wind Energy Forecasting Under False Data Injection Attacks Through Integration of CAE-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Accurate wind energy forecasting is paramount for the stability and reliability of modern power grids. This paper addresses a pioneering approach to wind energy forecasting within the context of cybersecurity, particularly focusing on the mitigation of False Data Injection (FDI) attacks. With the increasing reliance on smart grids and the integration of wind energy, the security of data used for forecasting has become paramount. Our research addresses the challenges posed by FDI attacks, which disrupt the accuracy of energy forecasts by maliciously altering input data. We propose a novel detection and mitigation framework that combines Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks (CAE-LSTM) to safeguard forecasting models against such cybersecurity threats. This framework not only identifies anomalies indicative of FDI attacks through advanced machine learning techniques but also ensures resilient forecasting by adapting predictions in response to detected anomalies. Our methodology is rigorously evaluated using real-world data and various attack scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining the integrity and reliability of wind energy forecasting. The outcomes of this research offer significant advancements in the security measures of energy systems, providing a robust model that enhances the accuracy and reliability of wind energy forecasts in the face of cyber threats.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Car Parking System Through Integrated Sensors and Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The growing urban population and increasing car ownership have led to a critical demand for efficient parking management solutions. This paper presents an IoT-enabled smart car parking system integrating IR sensors for vehicle detection, DHT22 for temperature and humidity monitoring, and MQ-2 sensors for hazardous gas detection. Key components include servo motors for automated gate control, OLED displays for real-time parking updates, and a mobile app utilizing MQTT protocol for seamless communication. The system offers real-time monitoring, automated slot management, and enhanced safety measures such as exhaust fan activation during high gas concentrations. Experimental results demonstrate improved parking efficiency, reduced emissions, and enhanced user experience, setting a new benchmark for smart parking systems in urban infrastructure.

articleTitle: Event and Anomaly Detection and Classification in Cyber-Physical Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Integrating digital and physical components in modern power grids has created new vulnerabilities, particularly from False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA). This complexity has also opened avenues for sophisticated cyberattacks, particularly False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA), which pose a significant threat to the stability and security of smart power grids. This research presents a novel approach to anomaly detection within the IEEE 39 bus system, with a specific emphasis on identifying FDIA in smart power grids. Leveraging the capabilities of Autoencoder-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, our study introduces a hybrid methodology that combines feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, and advanced classification techniques to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of anomaly detection. The proposed approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by effectively distinguishing between normal and malicious activities in the power grid, thereby mitigating the risks associated with FDIA. Extensive simulations were conducted to validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating its superior performance in detecting anomalies within the power system. The results indicate a marked improvement in detection accuracy, highlighting the potential of the proposed method as a robust solution for safeguarding smart power grids against cyber threats.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Gas Leak Detection and Fire Hazard Recognition System Using Image Processing for Household Safety Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) are widely used energy sources in households, but they pose significant safety risks. To mitigate these dangers, we have developed an IoT-based safety system designed for early detection and intervention. The system promptly identifies gas leaks and automatically shuts off the gas supply to prevent potential hazards. It is also equipped with a camera for detecting fires in vulnerable areas. Key features include real-time monitoring of gas concentrations and ambient temperature, displayed on an integrated interface, and the transmission of emergency alerts to users via the Blynk mobile application. The system is composed of a central control unit and multiple sub-units strategically placed in high-risk areas to enhance safety coverage. This cost-effective and efficient solution offers a proactive approach to preventing accidents, safeguarding lives, and protecting property.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation in Islanded Microgrids Using Linear Quadratic Gaussian Control
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller to regulate voltage in an islanded microgrid. Microgrids are becoming increasingly common because of their ability to incorporate renewable energy sources while improving power reliability. However, ensuring voltage stability during islanded operation remains a challenge, especially due to the fluctuating nature of renewable energy. The proposed LQG controller aims to address these challenges by minimizing voltage deviations, settling time, overshoot, and steady-state error. The controller is integrated into the microgrid inverter framework. The paper analyzes the controller's performance under various loading conditions and fault scenarios. The key contributions of this work are: • Proposing an LQG controller for voltage regulation in an island microgrid. • Demonstrate the effectiveness of the controller in reducing the settling time, overshoot, and steady-state error. • Evaluating the controller's robustness under different loading and fault conditions. This research contributes to the development of advanced control strategies to improve the stability of the voltage and overall performance of island microgrids.

articleTitle: Advancing Battery Management Systems: A Hybrid Approach Combining Unscented Kalman Filter and Machine Learning for Accurate State of Charge Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: As electric vehicle adoption and renewable energy integration rises globally; advanced battery monitoring is ever more essential. Precise determinations of State of Charge (SOC) and capacity are pivotal for optimizing performance over time, securing endurance, and maximizing efficiency. However, traditional approaches struggle with the nonlinear behavior and fading holding exhibited by modern battery arrays. This analysis explores merging machine learning methods, particularly Random Forest regression, with conventional techniques such as the UKF (Unscented Kalman Filter) and KF (Kalman Filter) for enhanced State of Charge and capacity projection. Using a sophisticated simulated Li-ion battery model comprising real-world factors like thermal effects and charging-discharging cycles, the examination contrasts the executions of the UKF and KF against the machine learning model. The results demonstrate that the machine learning-based approach, when combined with UKF and KF, significantly enhances State of Charge and capacity forecast precision. Namely, the hybrid strategy improves State of Charge estimation exactness to within 0.5% of real values and accomplishes a 12% advancement in capacity estimation precision contrasted with conventional techniques. These discoveries demonstrate the potential of joining machine learning with customary sifting strategies to fundamentally improve the exactness, dependability, and productivity of battery administration frameworks, guaranteeing preferable vitality use and RMSE of 68% expanding the operational lifetime of battery-subordinate advances.

articleTitle: PNA - Net: Leveraging Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Enhanced Pneumonia Detection from Chest X-Ray
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Pneumonia is a type of respiratory infection, and it is marked as one of the most deadly diseases in many countries. Sometimes moving to a medical center is difficult, b ut early diagnosis is very important. To encounter the problem, computer vision-based models can be a good solution. In this paper, we propose a custom CNN architecture named “PNA-Net” to detect pneumonia using chest X-ray images. We use 5856 images and split them into train and test sections with 5232 and 624, respectively. Our model attained 97.24% training accuracy and 97.90% validation accuracy. We made a comparison with some pretrained models; for instance, Resnet50, InceptionV3, VGG19, MobileNet, DenseNet121, VGG16, and Ensemble model, and their accuracies were 90.06%, 94.07%, 95.92%, 96.56%, 96.12%, 94.98%, and 94.84%, respectively. The overall study showed that our custom CNN model provided better accuracy than the previous works for the used dataset because of its tailored architecture with flexible h yperparameter tuning, outperformed all pretrained models, and can offer significant a ssistance in making clinical decisions and enhancing patient care.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Smart Greenhouse: Integrating Universal Interaction Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Agriculture is the largest employment sector in Bangladesh, making up 14.2% of GDP in 2017 and employing about 42.7% of the workforce. To support the GDP and grater employment, uses of the latest technology in agricultural areas are much more needed. Farmers still using the convention way to grow crops, which leads to less production, high labor cost, more manpower needed to monitor and maintenance the yield system. This study focuses on IoT-based smart greenhouse agricultural monitoring and automation, which provides farmers with real-time data and insights into a variety of topics such as data monitoring, controlling, automation crop yield, and cost effectiveness. An ESPS266-based hardware and Adafruit platform have been designed to monitor extracted data such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, automatic water irrigation and automatic hot air exhaust systems. The system's benefit is proved in a comprehensive manner through defined programming, hardware results, and data analysis, reducing the need for human monitoring and watering of the system, hot air will be expelled from the field, resulting in greater crop development up to 15-50% higher crop yield on the same field.

articleTitle: Advanced Color Sorting Conveyor System Using Arduino and TCS3200 Color Sensor for Precise Color Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This paper introduces an Arduino-based color-sorting conveyor belt system that automates object sorting by color. Employing a TCS3200 color sensor, an Arduino microcontroller detects red, green, and blue objects. Servo motors and IR sensors are utilized to sort objects accurately based on their color, while an LCD screen provides real-time feedback. The conveyor belt's motor controller regulates speed and direction, pausing during color detection for precise sorting. Experimental results demonstrate 100% efficiency in color detection and sorting, highlighting the system's potential for industrial automation applications.

articleTitle: Osprey Optimization Algorithm for Load Frequency Control in Renewable and Non-Renewable Energy Based Three-Area Power Generating System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The main objective of improving interconnected multi-area power systems in terms of automatic generation control (AGC) is making sure of reliable power production along with distribution, particularly in emergency situations. Despite technological progress, maintaining stable operation and efficient response to dynamic load changes remains a challenge. This study proposes A supplementary controller for regulating load frequency in an LFC system, aimed at improving system stability during sudden load fluctuations. The approach involves the optimal tuning of a PID controller applying the Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA). Consisting of three areas, a power system comprising of wind turbines, reheat thermal, and PV units, is developed to determine the optimal PID gain settings. Results show that the proposed OOA achieved rapid convergence, reaching optimal parameters by the 11<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> iteration, and provided a very low ITAE value of 0.07142.

articleTitle: Aircraft Simulation in Game Development Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The progress in technology has provided opportunities for innovative solutions to intricate challenges. One possible method is employing reinforcement learning to model flying trajectories in intricate environments. Game development is a discipline that involves intricate reasoning and dynamic interplay between the user and the game environment. By employing several gaming engines, developers are now able to replicate real-life situations through the implementation of diverse machine learning methods. Aircraft simulation in game creation using reinforcement learning involves creating a visual depiction of real-life settings where aircraft may navigate complex environments without direct input from a human user. Currently, reinforcement learning is not widely applied in game development, particularly in simulation-based path finding techniques. This algorithm approaches possess the efficacy and capacity to generate sophisticated neural networks capable of directing an agent to do certain tasks. The aim of this project is to create aircraft simulations for game development by utilizing reinforcement-learning techniques, so that it can provide a foundational idea of the usage of this algorithm in path-detection based decision-making techniques. The goal is to demonstrate the effectiveness of reinforcement learning in a real-world scenario, where the aircraft independently assesses and selects its flying trajectory. The system will undergo testing in three distinct phases, involving the utilization of Blender3D, Unity 3D, and Anaconda prompts. The results will then be compared using TensorFlow. Several training sessions will be conducted in various environments using the Anaconda environment to optimize the outcomes. In the latter stages of development, a dynamic user interface will be implemented to enhance the user's experience. The method is anticipated to produce 152% improved AI-trained data, which can be utilized for constructing extensive simulation and game-projects.

articleTitle: SciTexC: A Framework for Scientific Text Classification in Bengali using Transformer-Based Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Scientific text classification (STC) in NLP automatically categorizes texts into predefined scien-tific domains. Although there is enormous progress in STC regarding high-resource languages, it must be explored in low-resource languages, specifically Ben-gali. This study introduces a framework, SciTexC (Scientific Text Classifier), which uses a transformer-based technique that classifies Bengali texts into six scientific domains: Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Mathematics, and Others. A new corpus, STexD (scientific text dataset), containing 6000 Bengali texts, was also developed for classification tasks. Five transformer-based models were used to perform the task, including mBERT, dmBERT, Bangla BERT, Indic BERT, and XLM-RoBERTa. The evaluation results demonstrate that XLM-RoBERTa outperformed the other exploited models, achieving the highest F1 score (0.9158).

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Solar Powered Grinder Machine Operated by a BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The demand for grinded products is huge in both Bangladesh and overseas. The spice industry in Bangladesh alone has a market value of approximately 1300 crore taka. This huge market is dominated by a selected group of industries. Specifically, industrial-grade induction motors are vastly used in this sector, highlighting the contribution of motors in production processes. With such a vast market and immense potential, this paper aims to address the current situation and market demand of these kinds of products, focusing on how renewable energy technologies can transform this domain. This paper introduces the application of BLDC motors in grinding processes, showcasing a system capable of producing 5–6 kg of maize per hour using an 800W BLDC motor which is 1.5 times higher than the conventional motors. Using renewable energy as a power source enhances the systems' sustainability. The prospects of this system could be a source of income, reducing the cost of grinded products and improving accessibility, aligning with multiple sustainable development goals.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Real-Time Monitoring System for Indoor Air Purification with Gas Leakage Alerts
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Indoor air quality has become a critical concern in urban environments, where pollutants such as dust, volatile organic compounds, and hazardous gases can pose significant health risks. This paper presents the design and implementation of an IoT-based real-time monitoring system for indoor air purification, integrated with gas leakage alerts. The system utilizes a range of sensors, including DHT -22 for temperature and humidity, DM-5003 for dust detection, and MQ series sensors for hazardous gas detection, managed by an Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller. Wireless data transmission to the Blynk-IoT server via the NodeMCU-ESP8266 enables remote monitoring and control. The system has been evaluated in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing the Air Quality Index (AQI) from a high of 272 PPM to a safer level of 166 PPM. Additionally, the system successfully detected gas leaks, providing timely alerts. This system represents a significant advancement in maintaining healthy indoor environments.

articleTitle: A Forefront System for Sugarcane Leaf Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The agriculture sector has already seen a favorable advancement because of the involvement of machine learning (ML) methods. Sugarcane industry faces a gruesome drawback because of several types of leaf diseases. Nowadays, ML methods have come handy also to detect the diseases at the very early stage. Our work represents a cutting-edge deep learning method with a goal to classify five popular sugarcane leaf diseases: Bacterial Blight, Mosaic, RedRot, Rust, Yellow, and can also identify which one is Healthy. This study also conducts a comparative analysis of various state-of-the-art models, evaluating their training time, parameters, accuracy and model size using the same dataset. Based on this evaluation, the optimal model was selected for final evaluation. Several pre-trained models were modified to enhance speed and reduce storage requirements. The system can identify the disease category for every given sugarcane leaf image using the EfficientNetB0 model, which demonstrated the best performance, and also provides the probability of correct identification. Several preprocessing steps are involved such as removing noise, addressing missing data, and standardizing images to ensure maximum accuracy. The models were trained, validated, and tested on a dataset of 4,800 sugarcane leaf images from the Sugarcane Leaf Disease Dataset. Among all the models, EfficienNetB0, InceptionV3 and ResNet50 achieved high accuracy (98.75%, 98.54% and 98.54%, respectively). However, EfficienNetB0 was ultimately chosen due to its faster training, smaller size, and fewer parameters, making it ideal for this study.

articleTitle: Advanced Control Strategy for Mitigating Imbalances in Centralized Microgrids Using Grid-Forming Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Power instability in centralized microgrids remains a critical challenge due to fluctuating load demands and the dynamic nature of renewable energy sources. Traditional voltage and frequency control techniques often fail to tackle imbalances arising from uneven load distribution and dynamic generation patterns. To overcome this, the study introduces an advanced control strategy incorporating a novel centralized secondary control mechanism. This mechanism optimizes power management by factoring in intermittent levels, load-effective impedance, and voltage fluctuations, ensuring efficient voltage regulation and stability. The proposed approach aims to improve overall microgrid performance by dynamically balancing power distribution and enhancing control parameters. The effectiveness of the strategy is validated through simulation and experimental methods, demonstrating its ability to stabilize voltage and address power imbalances in centralized microgrids. The findings provide valuable insights for improving the reliability and efficiency of modern energy systems, particularly in dealing with voltage instability and variable load conditions in microgrid applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Optimization of Operation Cost and CO2 Emission Using Moth Flame Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: Power systems face the critical challenge of balancing increasing energy demands with the need to minimize operational costs and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. This paper presents a dynamic approach to optimizing operation costs and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions in power systems using the Moth Flame Optimization (MFO) algorithm. Applied to Bangladesh's west zone, the method minimizes total fuel costs while adhering to constraints on power balance, generation limits, and transmission losses. The study examines three case years-2018, 2021, and 2025-demonstrating that the MFO algorithm can reduce operational costs by 41% by 2025 and lower CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions by 2.16%. The algorithm effectively manages increased load demands through new power installations, such as solar and nuclear energy, ensuring grid stability and operational efficiency. The results confirm MFO's superiority in achieving significant economic and environmental benefits, highlighting its potential for broader application in power system optimization. This approach is particularly effective in dynamically adjusting to evolving grid requirements and challenges.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of ML Algorithms in Water Potability Prediction Aligned with SDGs
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: This research addresses the critical need for accurate water quality prediction, aligning with Clean Water and Sanitation (SDG 6) and Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3). Utilizing a diverse dataset of water quality attributes, we developed and evaluated multiple machine learning models to predict water potability, contributing to SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) through technological advancement. Our primary contribution is a Hyperparameter-Tuned Histogram Gradient Boosting Classifier, which outperformed several other algorithms, achieving an accuracy of 67%, a ROC-AUC score of 70%, and an F1-score of 66%. The study highlights challenges of class imbalance and feature distribution in water quality prediction, addressing aspects of SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) by improving urban water management. Our findings have significant implications for water resource management, supporting SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) through efficient resource utilization. While acknowledging limitations such as single dataset reliance, this research combines modern machine learning with comprehensive analysis to enhance water quality assessment. It contributes to SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) by providing a framework for collaboration between technology and environmental sectors. Future directions emphasize improving model performance and real-world applicability, potentially supporting SDG 13 (Climate Action) by enhancing resilience to water-related climate impacts.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting Using Deep Learning Algorithms with Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: The accurate forecasting of electrical load in short-term intervals is crucial for the efficient and secure operation of modern power systems. The dynamic nature of energy demand necessitates sophisticated forecasting techniques that can adapt to real-time changes, thereby optimizing power generation and distribution. This study proposes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model optimized using Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) to address the inherent non-linearities in load data and enhance predictive performance. The LSTM with HPO achieved a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 2.63%, substantially outperforming other models such as k-Nearest Neighbors (3.77%), Random Forest (3.46%), and Artificial Neural Networks (3.58%). It also recorded superior performance in Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), with values of 1.1423 and 1.0688, and an R2 of 0.9442. Additionally, experiments were conducted combining LSTM with other models to form hybrid architectures without applying HPO. These LSTM-based hybrids, such as RF-LSTM, consistently outperformed non-LSTM models, achieving a MAPE as low as 2.81%.

articleTitle: Size Optimization and Performance Analysis of Hybrid Biogas-Solar System for Energy-Efficient Dairy Farming
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST)
abstract: In Bangladesh, dairy industry plays a pivotal role in country's economic growth. Which is why integrating Biogas with Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems offers a reliable and sustainable energy solution for dairy farms. By supplementing solar energy in a hybridized setup, biogas ensures a consistent power supply, while also contributing to waste management and environmental sustainability. In this paper, area, load demand and biogas-solar generation potential in a conventional Bangladeshi dairy farm is studied. Then four renowned nature-inspired algorithms, Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA), and Polar Fox Optimization Algorithm (PFOA) are applied to optimize the design parameters of a Hybrid Biogas-Solar System for the farm. The primary objectives of optimization are to minimize costs, maximize energy output, and promote self-sustainability in dairy farming. The simulation results revealed that the system provided by the Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA) achieved a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of $0.045/kWh, a grid independent design with 0% loss of power supply probability (LPSP), and a payback period of 10 years and 4 months, making it the best-performing solution in terms of system reliability, self-sufficiency and energy efficiency compared to the GWO, WOA and PFOA.
